Please note that members of the public will be allowed to observe and/or address the City Council Meeting
of November 24, 2020, at 1:00 P.M. for closed session as follows:

  Contact the Office of the City Clerk at 310-412-5280 with any questions.

minutes_text:
Inglewood, California
  November 24, 2020

The City Council of the City of Inglewood, California held a regular meeting on
Tuesday, November 24, 2020, in the Council Chambers in City Hall of said City.

Mayor Butts called the City Council into Closed Session at the hour of 1:01 p.m.
The Acting City Clerk announced the presence of a quorum as follows:
  Present:  Mayor Butts, Council Members Dotson, Padilla,
  Morales, and Franklin; and
  Absent:  None.
City officials and personnel present for closed session were as follows:

  Artie Fields  City Manager
  Ken Campos  City Attorney
  Aisha Thompson  Acting City Clerk

PUBLIC COMMENTS REGARDING CLOSED SESSION ITEMS. Mayor
Butts inquired if there were any persons present who wished to address the City
Council on the Closed Session Items.

There was no response.

Mayor Butts recessed the City Council at the hour of 1:02 p.m. for Closed Session
Item Nos. CS-1, CS-2, and CS-3.

  *****************

Following the Pledge of Allegiance to the flag of our Country, Mayor Butts called
the City Council into joint session with the Successor Agency, Housing
Authority, and Joint Powers Authority at the hour of 2:03 p.m.
The Acting City Clerk/ Successor Agency Secretary / Housing Authority
Secretary / Joint Powers Authority Secretary announced the presence of a quorum
as follows:

  Present:  Mayor/Successor Agency Chairman/Housing
  Authority Chairman/Joint Powers Authority
  Chairman Butts, Council Members/Successor
  Agency Members/Housing Authority Members/
  Joint Powers Authority Members Dotson, Padilla,
  Morales, and Franklin; and
  Absent:  None.

City/Successor Agency / Housing Authority/Joint Powers Authority officials and
personnel present were as follows:
  Aisha L. Thompson  Acting City Clerk /Secretary*
  Artie Fields  City Manager/Executive Director*
  Ken Campos  City Attorney/General Counsel*
  David Esparza  Asst. City Manager/CFO
  Jacquelyn Gordon  Staff Assistant

* Serves as indicated for the Successor Agency, Housing Authority, and Joint
Powers Authority.

PUBLIC COMMENTS – AGENDA ITEMS. Mayor/Successor Agency
Chairman/Housing Authority Chairman/Joint Powers Authority Chairman Butts
inquired if there were any persons present who wished to address the City
Council/Successor Agency/Housing Authority/Joint Powers Authority on any
item on the Agendas, other than the Public Hearing.

  1
 November 24, 2020

  Caller (Name Unknown) spoke on Agenda Items Nos. 3, 6, 11, 12, and O-1.

  Gil Mathieu, District 4, spoke on the Warrants and Bills.

 142.9  PAYMENT OF WARRANTS AND BILLS. It was moved by Council Member
  /Successor Agency Member / Housing Authority Member Franklin, and seconded
  by Council Member /Successor Agency Member / Housing Authority Member
  Padilla that the demands presented to the City Council/Successor
  Agency/Housing Authority dated November 20, 2020, in the amount of
  $3,745,688.10 are hereby allowed, and the City Clerk /Successor Agency
  Secretary/Housing Authority Secretary is hereby authorized to certify upon said
  registers that said demands are so approved. The motion was carried by the
  following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members/Successor Agency Members/Housing Authority
  Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Franklin, and Mayor/Successor
  Agency Chairman/Housing Authority Chairman Butts; and
  Noes: None.

 301  PUBLIC HEARING HELD – ORDINANCE NO. 21-03 INTRODUCED -
  AMENDING INGLEWOOD MUNICIPAL CODE CHAPTER 12
  INCLUDING ZONING CODE AMENDMENT 2020-003 TO MODIFY
  SELF-STORAGE FACILITY REGULATIONS CITYWIDE. The Acting
  City Clerk announced the next scheduled matter was to consider an ordinance
  amending Inglewood Municipal Code Chapter 12 (Planning and Zoning),
  including Zoning Code Amendment 2020-003 (ZCA 2020-003) to modify self-
  storage facility regulations citywide, that notices were given in the time, form and
  manner as required by law, an affidavit is on file, and no communications were
  received.

  Mindy Wilcox, Planning Manager, presented the staff report dated November 24,
  2020.

  Mayor Butts inquired if there were any persons present who wished to address the
  City Council on this matter.

  Caller (Name Unknown) commented that housing and green space should be
  developed, and there is no need for more storage facilities.

  Gil Mathieu, District 4, commented he doesn’t think more storage facilities are
  needed.

  Norman Lee asked to receive support for Black Businesses who rent commercial
  properties.

  Mayor Butts closed the public comments portion at the hour of 2:30 p.m.

  After Council discussion, it was moved by Council Member Franklin, and
  seconded by Council Member Morales that the City Council does hereby affirm
  Categorical Exemption 2020-096. The motion was carried by the following roll
  call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Franklin, and Mayor Butts;
  and
  Noes: None.

  It was moved by Council Member Franklin, and seconded by Council Member
  Morales that further reading be waived. The motion was carried by the following
  roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Franklin, and Mayor Butts;
  and
  Noes: None.

  2
 November 24, 2020

  Thereupon, Ordinance No. 21-03 entitled:

  AN ORDINANCE OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF
  INGLEWOOD, CALIFORNIA, TO ADOPT AN EXEMPTION (EA-CE-
  2020-096) AND APPROVE ZONING CODE AMENDMENT 2020-003
  (ZCA-2020-003) TO AMEND ARTICLES 1,8,11.1,19 AND 25 OF
  CHAPTER 12 (PLANNING AND ZONING) OF THE INGLEWOOD
  MUNICIPAL CODE TO MODIFY SELF-STORAGE FACILITY
  REGULATIONS CITYWIDE.

  was introduced by Mayor Butts.

 131  PUBLIC HEARING HELD – RESOLUTION NO. 21-03 ADOPTED –
  AMENDING FISCAL YEAR 2020-2021 ANNUAL ACTION PLAN TO
  REALLOCATE PROGRAM FUNDS FOR THE MINOR HOME REPAIR
  PROGRAM. The Acting City Clerk announced that the next scheduled matter is
  a public hearing to consider taking final action on the proposed substantial
  amendments to the Fiscal Year 2020-2021 Annual Action Plan to reallocate
  program funds for the Minor Home Repair Program, that notice has been given in
  the time, form, and manner as required by law, an affidavit is on file, and no
  communications were received.

  Roberto Chavez, HUD Manager, presented the staff report dated November 24,
  2020.

  Mayor Butts inquired if there were any persons present who wished to address the
  City Council on this matter.

  There were no comments.

  It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council Member
  Franklin that the City Council does hereby adopt Resolution No. 21-29 entitled:

  A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF
  INGLEWOOD, CALIFORNIA ADOPTING A SUBSTANTIAL
  AMENDMENT TO THE FISCAL YEAR 2020-2021 ANNUAL
  ACTION PLAN TO INCLUDE FUNDING FOR THE MINOR HOME
  REPAIR PROGRAM

  The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Franklin, and Mayor Butts;
  and
  Noes: None.

  and
  Noes: None.

  Member Franklin that the Minutes for the City Council Meetings held on June 23,

 101  ORDINANCE NO 21-02 ADOPTED – CONTRIBUTION LIMITS FOR
  THE CITY OF INGLEWOOD ELECTED OFFICIALS AND
  CANDIDATES.  Staff report dated November 24, 2020, was presented
  recommending adoption of Ordinance No 21-02 establishing maximum campaign
  contribution limits for the City of Inglewood Elected Officials and Candidates of
  $100,000 per donor election cycle.

  It was moved by Council Member Padilla, and seconded by Council Member
  Dotson that further reading be waived The motion was carried by the following
  roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Franklin, and;
  Noes: None; and
  Absent: Mayor Butts.

  Council Member Morales recessed the City Council Meeting at 2:42 p.m.

  Mayor Butts reconvened the City Council Meeting at 2:45 p.m.

  Mayor Butts asked if there were any comments from the Council to address
  Agenda Item No. O-1 (Adoption of Ordinance No. 21-02).

  Council Member Morales, clarified Agenda Item No. O-1 was being addressed
  due to the adoption of new State Laws to identify limits for candidates, and the

  7
 November 24, 2020

  City Council had not addressed it in the city of Inglewood. Now the public would
  be made aware and gain clarity.

  Council Member Franklin commented on Agenda Item No. O-1, making mention
  of the last sentence in the staff report, which allows the City to retain local
  control, and not rely on the State’s default restrictions.

  Mayor Butts commented that Inglewood, like many other cities in the past, had no
  limits on campaign contributions. He further commented that Ordinance No. 21-
  02 is in response to the State’s law, allowing cities to set their limits for donations
  instead of becoming a mandate. The Mayor stated there was a Federal Court
  decision that stated “Corporations are entities, and they get to donate as a form of
  free speech,” which means they can donate unlimited funds of money to political
  action committees to determine the outcome of elections. He commented unions
  have the same power because they can collectively pull money, and that’s great
  because it’s all free speech. The Mayor continued by stating, it’s unfair for a
  candidate not to have the right to raise sufficient sums of money, to be
  competitive in a race; so the only thing that was changed from having unlimited
  donations, the City Council put a cap on the donations set at $100,000. Lastly, he
  commented that the Council is choosing for the City’s Independence instead of
  relying on heavily funded entities to allow candidates to be competitive in an
  election.

  It was moved by Council Member Franklin, and seconded by Council Member
  Morales, that Ordinance No. 21-02 entitled:

  AN ORDINANCE OF THE CITY OF INGLEWOOD, CALIFORNIA
  ESTABLISHING CAMPAIGN FINANCE CONTRIBUTION LIMITS
  BY ADDING SECTION 2-247.1 (CAMPAIGN CONTRIBUTION
  LIMITS AND REGULATIONS) TO ARTICLE 8 (COUNCIL
  DISTRICTS MEETINGS CITY FACILITIES) OF CHAPTER 2
  (ADMINISTRATION) OF THE INGLEWOOD MUNICIPAL CODE.

  which was introduced at the meeting held on November 17, 2020, be adopted.
  The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Franklin, and Mayor Butts;
  and
  Noes: None.
